const-1986.title: Constitution of the Republic of Liberia (January 6, 1986)
const-1986.note: Official English text as filed with WIPO Lex (lr003en.pdf). Arts. 37 (by-elections), 45-48 (Senate and House), 50 (President), 54(d) (appointed county and subdivision officials), 56(b) (chiefs), 80(d)-(e) (constituencies), 83 (election day and majority), 91-92 (amendment by referendum).

elections-law.title: Title 11, Elections Law (New Elections Law, approved September 29, 1986, with amendments through the Elections Act of 2004 and the 2004 Electoral Reform Law)
elections-law.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Liberia (Liberian Codes Revised, Vol. II)
elections-law.note: Published by Authority, Bureau of Printing, Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Pages 238-336 of Liberian Codes Revised Vol. II; the 2004 Electoral Reform Law of the National Transitional Legislative Assembly is reproduced from page 316.

sc-mayors-2008.title: CDC et al. v. Executive Branch et al., Opinion of the Supreme Court, October Term 2007 (decided January 11, 2008)
sc-mayors-2008.note: Holds the 1979 Act Regulating the Time of Election of City Mayors unconstitutional under Article 54(d) and repealed by implication from January 6, 1986.

sc-threshold-2010.title: In re Petition for Declaratory Judgment on the Constitutionality of a Joint Resolution on the Setting of an Electoral Threshold, Opinion of the Supreme Court (decided October 11, 2010)
sc-threshold-2010.note: Joint Resolution LEG-002 (2010), approved July 29, 2010, kept the 64 House seats and added nine constituencies in six of the fifteen counties; the Court quashed the writ as a political question, so the 73 constituencies stood for 2011.

nec-results.title: Election results (national tally)

classes.name: Election of the President and Vice President
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Art. 50: six-year term, at most two terms; Art. 83(b): absolute majority, else a runoff)
classes.note: Joint ticket elected nationwide by two-round absolute majority (Art. 83(b); Elections Law § 4.15(a)). Tallied by polling place and precinct, then by electoral district and county.

cadence.runoff_rule: Absolute majority of valid votes, else a runoff between the top two on the second Tuesday after the first-round results are announced
cadence.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Art. 83(a): "second Tuesday in October of each election year"; Art. 83(c): returns declared within fifteen days)

access.evidence: Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403) to scripts; the national tally page lists county results for 2023

dates.note: First election under the 1986 Constitution, held by the Special Elections Commission under the People's Redemption Council before the Constitution took effect on January 6, 1986.
Special election under the Abuja peace accords, one national constituency.
Runoff delayed from November 7 by the Supreme Court's hearing of the first-round complaint.
Next regular election: the second Tuesday in October of the election year (Art. 83(a)).

classes.name: Election of the President under the 1847 Constitution
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Art. 94-95: transitional provisions replacing the suspended 1847 Constitution)
classes.note: Presidents were elected under the 1847 Constitution from 1847 (two-year terms, later four and eight) until the April 12, 1980 coup suspended it. Returns were canvassed by the Legislature and printed, when at all, in legislative journals and handbills.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes the 1847-1975 presidential returns; the canvasses sit in legislative journals and handbills that are not online, and the National Elections Commission's site holds only post-1985 results and refuses automated clients.

dates.note: First presidential election under the 1847 Constitution.
Last presidential election before the 1980 coup.

classes.name: Election of the House of Representatives
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Art. 48: six-year term, elected in the legislative constituencies of the counties; Art. 80(d): at most one hundred constituencies)
classes.note: Single-member districts by plurality since 2005 (2004 Electoral Reform Law § 1.4; Elections Law § 4.15(c)); 64 districts in 2005 and 73 since 2011. The 1997 House was chosen by national-list proportional representation.

dates.note: Seats filled by proportional representation from one national constituency under the 1997 special elections arrangements.

dates.quote: § 4.2: "For the 2005 elections, the number of members of the House of Representatives shall be fixed at sixty-four (64)." § 1.4: single member electoral districts
"maintained the current 64 Legislative seats and at the same time allotted nine (9) new Legislative constituencies" (Joint Resolution LEG-002 (2010), for the 2011 elections)

classes.name: By-election to the House of Representatives
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Art. 37: by-election within 90 days of the Commission's notice of a vacancy)
classes.note: Called by the National Elections Commission within 90 days of a vacancy, unless the vacancy falls within 90 days of a general election (Art. 37; Elections Law § 1.2(h)).

cadence.vacancy_rule: The presiding officer notifies the Commission within 30 days; the Commission holds the by-election within 90 days, unless the vacancy arises within 90 days of a general election

classes.name: Election of the Senate
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Art. 45: two senators per county, nine-year terms; Art. 46: staggered categories)
classes.note: Each county elects two senators. In 1985 and 2005 both seats were filled at once and the runner-up's seat ran a six-year first term (Art. 46; 2004 Electoral Reform Law § 1.3), so since 2011 half the counties' seats (one per county) fall due in alternating three- and six-year gaps: 2011, 2014, 2020, 2023, 2029, 2032. Plurality per seat since 2011.

cadence.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Arts. 45-46 and 83(a); seats filled in 2014 and 2023, with the general election since 2023)
https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Arts. 45-46; seats filled in 2011 and 2020, the midterm cycle (December 8 in 2020))

dates.note: Two senators for each of the 13 counties then existing.
Seats filled by proportional representation from one national constituency under the 1997 special elections arrangements.

dates.quote: § 1.3: "The two candidates who obtain the highest and second highest numbers of valid votes cast in the county shall be elected"; § 1.2(l): "each of the fifteen counties"

dates.note: Second-category seats after their first six-year term (Art. 46).
First-category seats after nine years; postponed from October 14, 2014 during the Ebola epidemic.
Midterm senatorial election, held with the 2020 constitutional referendum.
Next midterm senatorial election: the seats filled in December 2020 expire after nine years (Art. 45).

classes.name: By-election to the Senate
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Arts. 37 and 45: a by-elected senator serves the remainder of the term)
classes.note: Called within 90 days of a vacancy (Art. 37) for the remainder of the term (Art. 45).

cadence.vacancy_rule: The presiding officer notifies the Commission within 30 days; the Commission holds the by-election within 90 days, unless the vacancy arises within 90 days of a general election

classes.name: Election of the Legislature under the 1847 Constitution
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Arts. 94-95: transitional provisions replacing the suspended 1847 Constitution)
classes.note: Senate and House of Representatives of the First Republic, elected by county until the April 12, 1980 coup.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes the First Republic's legislative returns; they survive only in printed legislative journals and handbills that are not online.

classes.name: Constitutional referendum
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Art. 91: ratified by two-thirds of the registered voters voting in a referendum; Art. 92: each proposal voted on separately)
classes.note: The 1984 referendum adopted the Constitution. The August 23, 2011 referendum put four propositions; the Supreme Court read the two-thirds rule against valid votes and held Proposition 4 (plurality for elections other than the presidency) adopted. All eight propositions of December 8, 2020 fell short of two-thirds.

cadence.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Art. 91: not sooner than one year after the Legislature's action)

classes.name: Referendum under the 1847 Constitution
classes.note: Ratification of the 1847 Constitution and its later amendments by popular vote.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes the 1847-1980 referendum returns; they survive only in printed legislative records that are not online.

classes.name: Election of Paramount Chiefs
classes.locator: https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/en/legislation/details/8556 (Art. 56(b): "There shall be elections of Paramount, Clan and Town Chiefs by the registered voters in their respective localities, to serve for a term of six years")
classes.note: Six-year terms (Art. 56(b); Elections Law § 1.7), candidates at least 30 (§ 1.8). The Commission conducts chieftaincy elections and is the judge of their contests (§ 2.9(q), (t)); since the civil war chiefs have mostly been appointed or chosen locally pending elections.
classes.disposition_reason: The National Elections Commission has published no chieftaincy returns: none appear on its results pages, and no official register lists the chiefdoms, clans, and towns or the dates their chiefs were last elected.

cadence.locator: https://liblaw.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/NEW-ELECTIONS-LAW.pdf (page 250, § 1.7: "Election of chiefs shall be held every six (6) years by registered voters of the chiefdom, clan, and town")

classes.name: Election of City Mayors and Common Councils
classes.locator: https://liblaw.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/CDC-et-al.-v.-Executive-Branch-et-al.-2008.pdf (pages 5-6: the 1979 Act "is opposed to the plain terms of Article 54(d)" and city-charter provisions for elected mayors were "repealed by implication" on January 6, 1986)
classes.note: The 1979 Act Regulating the Time of Election of City Mayors set quadrennial elections on the second Tuesday in November, starting November 1979; earlier charters elected mayors on their own dates. Since January 6, 1986 the President appoints mayors with the Senate's consent (Art. 54(d)), so no class remains open.
classes.disposition_reason: Abolished in 1986. No official body publishes the returns of the city elections held under city charters and the 1979 Act; they survive only in handbills and local records.

cadence.locator: https://liblaw.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/CDC-et-al.-v.-Executive-Branch-et-al.-2008.pdf (page 4, Act of August 9, 1979, § 1: "elected quadrennially on the second Tuesday in November")

dates.note: Second Tuesday in November 1979, the date the 1979 Act fixed for all city mayors.

classes.name: Party primaries
classes.locator: https://liblaw.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/NEW-ELECTIONS-LAW.pdf (§ 2.9: the Commission's powers cover public elections and referenda, not party nominations)
classes.note: Parties and coalitions choose their candidates under their own constitutions; the Commission only accepts their nominations.
classes.disposition_reason: No state-run nominating contest exists: the National Elections Commission administers no primaries, and parties publish no official returns.
